_doc: Role-binding precedence graph. Machine-readable companion to top-level-runtime-contract.md §3. Consumed by conformance-matrix.js (kernel fixtures, gate 'role-binding') and by the live dispatch runtime. 'sources' is TOTAL over every 'order' entry except UNBOUND, and key names align with 'order' exactly. Every source also carries 'applies_to_actor' — the graph is TOTAL over {source × actor_kind}, not just over 'order'. A dispatched_worker is bindable ONLY by sources whose applies_to_actor includes 'dispatched_worker' (today: validated_workorder_or_cli alone); explicit_user and explicit_top_level_helm are top_level_session-ONLY sources. A dispatched_worker presenting either of those is a CATEGORY ERROR, not a legitimate bind, and must resolve BLOCK (fail-closed) — never PASS as though it had resolved through the precedence order.

explicit_user._meaning: An explicit, in-session user/operator instruction — the OPERATOR's own direct instruction (a trusted human), categorically different from ambient repo prose. Precedence order position #1. applies_to_actor = top_level_session ONLY: a dispatched_worker presenting this source is a category error, not a legitimate bind.

validated_workorder_or_cli._meaning: A validated WorkOrder field or CLI/dispatch binding. 'Validated' means the TRUSTED dispatch bridge (scripts/dispatch-claude.js / scripts/dispatch-agent.js) has ACTIVELY validated it -- schema conformance against workorder-min.schema.json AND an authority/provenance check, BOTH performed BY the trusted layer itself -- not merely that the binding transited the bridge (transit alone is insufficient) and never a self-asserted claim — see top-level-runtime-contract.md §3 P3.2 for the full provenance definition. Precedence order position #2. applies_to_actor = dispatched_worker AND top_level_session: this is the ONLY source a dispatched_worker may bind through.

explicit_top_level_helm._meaning: An explicit top-level runtime (helm) binding. Precedence order position #3; the ONLY source for the top-level human-facing session default (top_level_default_binding_source = helm_only). applies_to_actor = top_level_session ONLY: a dispatched_worker presenting this source is a category error, not a legitimate bind — see fixtures/role-binding/worker-helm-binding-category-error.json.

agents_md._meaning: The neutral, provider-neutral handbook every provider auto-loads — ambient prose, NOT an ordered binding source (not in 'order' above). CORE-3: ambient prose can never itself manufacture a binding, for ANY actor_kind (can_bind:false makes applies_to_actor moot, but it is listed for both so the {source × actor_kind} graph stays total).

repo_prose._meaning: Any other ambient repository text (stale worktree copies, handoff prompts, etc.) — same CORE-3 refusal as agents_md, for ANY actor_kind.

notes.CORE-1: Dispatched workers NEVER default to binding as the President (alex-alpha) when unbound; worker_default_when_unbound = FAIL_CLOSED is the machine-readable form of this invariant. This ALSO covers a worker that presents a source outside its applies_to_actor scope (e.g. explicit_top_level_helm_binding) — that is a category error and must resolve BLOCK exactly like the unbound case, never PASS as alex-alpha.
notes.CORE-3: repo_prose.can_bind = false and agents_md.can_bind = false — neutral, provider-neutral, AMBIENT prose (root AGENTS.md, ambient CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md shims, any stale worktree copy, any handoff prompt) can NEVER manufacture a binding. CORE-3 is a restriction on ambient/neutral PROSE specifically — it is NOT a claim that only a validated WorkOrder/CLI binding or an explicit top-level helm binding can bind a role at all. Per the 'order' above, explicit_user.can_bind = true: the operator's own direct, in-session instruction IS a legitimate binding source (order position #1), categorically different from ambient repo prose. All three of explicit_user, validated_workorder_or_cli, and explicit_top_level_helm can bind (subject to their applies_to_actor scope); only agents_md and repo_prose (ambient prose) cannot bind at all, for any actor.
notes.top_level_default: The TOP-LEVEL human-facing session defaults to alex-alpha, but ONLY via an explicit helm binding (top_level_default_binding_source = helm_only) — never via ambient/neutral prose. Dispatched workers are UNBOUND-fail-closed; the operator's own top-level session is NOT left unbound.
notes.actor_scoping: explicit_user and explicit_top_level_helm are top_level_session-ONLY sources (applies_to_actor = ["top_level_session"]); validated_workorder_or_cli is the ONLY source a dispatched_worker may bind through (applies_to_actor includes "dispatched_worker"). A dispatched_worker presenting explicit_user_instruction or explicit_top_level_helm_binding is a CATEGORY ERROR — the presented source exists and can_bind:true in the abstract, but does not apply to this actor_kind — and must resolve BLOCK, never resolve through the precedence order as if it were a top_level_session. See fixtures/role-binding/worker-helm-binding-category-error.json.
